identity.name: Polydextrose
identity.chemical_class: Synthetic randomly bonded glucose polymer (polymerized dextrose)

function.mechanism: Mostly not absorbed intact in the small intestine; partially fermented in the colon to short-chain fatty acids, providing bulk and reduced caloric impact compared with sugars.
common_food_categories: frozen dairy desserts and fruit ices

adi.basis: EFSA (2021) concluded there is no need for a numerical ADI for polydextrose (E1200).

efsa.key_finding: No concern regarding genotoxicity or carcinogenicity; no need for a numerical ADI.

fda.notes: Polydextrose is listed as a direct food additive under specified conditions of use and exclusions (including baby foods and infant formulas) in this CFR section; this citation is not a GRAS listing.

adi.basis: JECFA database entry lists ADI as 'not specified' for polydextrose.

concerns.summary: High acute intakes can cause gastrointestinal intolerance (gas, bloating, laxation/diarrhea), consistent with partial colonic fermentation.
Recent human trials focused on gut/constipation outcomes and infant formula tolerance did not identify major new systemic toxicity signals in reviewed abstracts.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2021 found no concern regarding genotoxicity.
EFSA 2021 found no concern regarding carcinogenicity from available long-term studies.
JECFA ADI listed as not specified.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA did not establish a numerical ADI, so standard ADI exceedance comparison is not directly applicable; highest modeled exposures were in younger age groups.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations are favorable (EFSA no numerical ADI needed; JECFA ADI not specified; FDA-approved uses under 21 CFR 172.841), but dose-related GI intolerance is credible at high acute intakes.
key_factors: US CFR permits use with explicit conditions
GI side effects occur at higher bolus doses
